# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29 (Bi-Vb Pc29)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc29
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29
**Title (English, from literature):** Letting the robe season expire
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kālaatikkamana-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 29) governs the proper period for the division of robe-cloth among nuns. According to the rule, a nun who without good reason causes the proper robe season to expire—by delaying or hindering the distribution of robe material—commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the background narrative (*nidāna*), the nun Thullanandā prompted the Saṅgha to postpone the distribution of robes in uncertain expectation of additional cloth promised vaguely by a lay family; however, the expected material was never actually provided, leaving the distribution needlessly obstructed [Hüsken 1997]. Modern scholarship classifies this rule as a specialized counterpart to Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 26: while rule 26 prohibits preventing the community from receiving robes altogether, rule 29 prohibits ungrounded delays in dividing or receiving robe material [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels in Buddhist Vinaya literature include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (rule 29), alongside corresponding pācittiya rules across multiple sectarian traditions: the Dharmaguptaka (Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha Pc 110), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 185), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 135), and Mūlasarvāstivāda in Chinese (Pc 146) and Tibetan translation (Pc 169). Computational reuse matches identified by DharmaNexus align with this broad preservation, showing notable text alignments with Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* texts and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, extensive phrasing is shared with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, most prominently Pācittiya 27, 53, and 26 [DharmaNexus].
